newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press - Oct 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- AIRLINES WIN 150 MILLON STG CUTS IN CHARGES FROM BAA

The airlines which use airports operated by BAA, including Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted, have won a 150 million stg reduction in take-off and landing charges over the next five years after rejecting proposals for even bigger cuts. The airlines were worried that the offer of larger reductions, raised in a document by the Civil Aviation Authority, would make it more difficult for BAA to finance investment in Heathrow's Terminal Five and other programmes.
-- BIDDERS TARGET POWER GROUPS

Two American utilities are considering bids for British electricity companies. Houston Industries and Duke Power are eager to buy British electricity companies. This has increased takeover speculation in the water and electricity industry. Ian Lang, trade and industry secretary, is expected to allow Severn Trent and Wessex Water to make bids for South West Water.
-- BAIRD FOCUSES ON M AND S AFTER SUDDENS REJIG

As part of a restructuring plan announced by chief executive David Suddens, the textile group William Baird is planning to close up to three British factories at the cost of 500 jobs and transfer some production overseas. Baird will concentrate on supplying Marks and Spencer with clothing, shedding contract work with other high street customers. It aims to bolster its Windsmoor and Dannimac branded clothing side.
THE TIMES
-- HALIFAX INVESTOR IN LINE FOR 1,000 STG WINDFALL

When Halifax building society becomes a bank in June next year borrowers and savers will be in line for a bonus of 1,000 stg. The payout will be in free shares, to be issued to all qualifying members when the society converts to a public listed company with a market capitalisation of ten billion stg. Members will be sent full details in January and will be given an indication of the likely price range of Halifax shares, based on prevailing market conditions.
-- 50 MILLION STG SHORTFALL IN NATIONAL SAVINGS BOOKS

According to a report by the National Audit Office, the Government's savings arm has an unexplained 50 million stg black hole. Head of the NAO Sir John Bourn lists a catalogue of serious accounting errors at National Savings, which looks after more than 57 billion stg on behalf of 30 million people. Sir John is concerned over the accounting procedures for looking after savers' cash at National Savings, which raises money from the public to help fund the Government's borrowing requirements.
-- SHARPLES NETS 57 MILLION DOLLARS FROM ICV SALE

Former head of the City watchdog Securities and Futures Authority, Christopher Sharples, is set to gain 57 million dollars from the sale of ICV, the company which runs the Stock Exchange's company news service. ICV was set up by Mr Sharples in 1981 and is being acquired by Primark, the US business information company, for 105 million dollars. Primark and ICV are to team up with Dow Jones in an Anglo-American financial information partnership to challenge Reuters' dominance of the five billion dollar market place.
THE GUARDIAN
-- COUNCILS TURN SCREW ON MORGAN GRENFELL

In the wake of the Peter Young affair local government treasurers are demanding answers from the asset management arm of Morgan Grenfell about its security and systems. A withdrawal of the authorities' pension fund business would be devastating to the firm, which already faces the loss of Westminster City Council's 200 million stg mandate. The council's investment committee has asked other fund managers to tender for the work, even though, according to city chief executive Bill Roots, Morgan Grenfell's results have been "first class".
-- ALLEGED BP 'FIXER' IN COLOMBIA NAMED

The European Parliament has named British Petroleum's alleged "inside man' within the Colombian government. Labour MEP Richard Howitt has said that Ramon Morino is one of a number of former and current BP employees inside the administration who smooth the agreement of environmental permits. Mr Howitt's claim forms part of a string of allegations, which are all denied by BP, such as BP being involved in human-rights abuses and environmental damage in Colombia.
-- REGULATORS NEED BETTER ADVICE, CBI INSISTS

The CBI has said that privatised utility regulators should have permanent expert advisory boards but should not be merged or replaced by a single super regulator. The CBI also confirmed its opposition to Labour's plans for a windfall tax on utility profits. This intervention comes after the Government failed to include new competition legislation in the Queen's Speech. CBI director-general Peter Agar said that advisory boards are needed because regulation has become individual and personalised.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- ARGOS VICTORY OPENS WAY FOR FLOOD OF VAT CLAIMS

The European Court of Justice has decided that Customs and Excise was wrong in charging VAT tax on the full price of goods which were sold at a discount by Argos and Elida Gibbs. Accountants suggest repayment could be 400 million stg on overpaid VAT, however, the Treasury says the amount will be 200 million stg. The accountancy firm Coopers and Lybrand say that 40 billion stg is being claimed back from Customs for VAT wrongly imposed.
-- NERVOUS INVESTORS WIPE 1.4 BILLION STG OFF VALUE OF BSKYB

Rupert Murdoch's confirmation of plans to raise funds through a preference share issue convertible into BSkyB shares has led to a drop in shares of the satellite broadcaster for the second day running. Analysts say Murdoch's plans to mortgage part of his BSkyB stake suggests he believes the shares had reached their likely high, and that it was an opportune time to raise fresh funds to finance his other global media ventures.
-- CHEMICALS SLUMP HAMMERS ICI PROFITS

Third-quarter profits at ICI have seen a slump following falling bulk chemical prices, however, shares closed 17 pence stg higher. Chairman Sir Ronald Hampel said that the pace of economic activity remained uneven and there is no significant change expected before the end of the year. He said this was evidence of the end of a widespread destocking which began in mid-1995, and that sales volumes increased in almost all businesses in the third quarter. BMC +44-171-377-1742 END
